answer_text: The Giant is called selfish because he did not let the children play in his garden. He drove them out, built a high wall around his garden, and put up a board that read 'Trespassers will be prosecuted.'
final_answer: Thus, the Giant's actions of excluding the children from his garden define his selfishness.

question_text: (i) When spring came, it was still winter in the garden. What does winter stand for or indicate here? (ii) Winter has been presented like a story with its own characters and their activities. Describe the story in your own words.

parts.part_text: When spring came, it was still winter in the garden. What does winter stand for or indicate here?
parts.answer_text: In the story, winter stands for a negative, desolate and lifeless environment. In this environment, trees and flowers do not blossom. Here, winter also refers to an atmosphere of depression and laziness. Since birds did not sing, children did not play and spring did not visit the garden, winter prolonged its stay in the garden.
parts.final_answer: Thus, winter symbolizes the absence of joy and life in the garden.

parts.part_text: Winter has been presented like a story with its own characters and their activities. Describe the story in your own words.
parts.answer_text: When spring came, the birds did not sing as there were no children. The trees too did not blossom. At a particular instance, a flower put its head out from the grass. However, when it saw the notice board put up by the giant, it felt sad and sorry for the children, got back inside the grass, and went off to sleep. On the other hand, snow and frost were very happy. While the snow covered the grass, the frost fell on all the trees. They invited the North Wind to stay with them, and later even the Hail was asked to visit. The Hail rattled the roof of the castle every day until some of it started breaking, and then it ran round the garden again and again as fast as it could.
parts.final_answer: The story illustrates the desolation of the garden during winter and the joy of winter elements.

difficulty_reasoning: Requires interpretation and summarization of the text.

question_text: The little child's hands and feet had marks of nails. Who does the child remind you of? Give a reason for your answer.
answer_text: The child reminds one of Jesus Christ. When the Giant met the little child for the second time, he saw imprints of nails on his palms and feet. When Christ was crucified, nails were dug into his palms and feet. He had sacrificed his life for humanity, so that the sins of the world would be washed away. That is why the child told the Giant that those were the wounds of love.
final_answer: Therefore, the child symbolizes sacrifice and love, akin to Jesus Christ.

question_text: (i) The Giant saw a most wonderful sight. What did he see? (ii) What did he realise on seeing it?

parts.part_text: The Giant saw a most wonderful sight. What did he see?
parts.answer_text: The Giant saw that the children had entered the garden through a small hole in the wall, and were sitting on the branches of trees. There was a child on every tree. The trees had covered themselves with blossoms as they were glad to have the children back. The birds were flying about and twittering in delight, and the flowers and grass were laughing out loud.
parts.final_answer: Thus, the Giant witnessed the joy and life returning to his garden.

parts.part_text: What did he realise on seeing it?
parts.answer_text: He realised that spring did not come to his garden because he had prevented the children from playing in his garden. He realised that he was selfish not to allow the children to play in his garden.
parts.final_answer: Therefore, he recognized the consequences of his selfishness.

difficulty_reasoning: Requires interpretation of the Giant's realization.
